claims.claim_vi: The source describes steps 1 to 8: capture, compress and encode (H.264), segment, send to a streaming server that produces multiple bitrates (adaptive bitrate streaming), push to CDN edge servers, viewers decode and play, optional storage for replay.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: The source names RTMP, HLS and DASH as standard live-streaming protocols and says HLS and DASH both support adaptive bitrate streaming.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: The source says Apple devices accept only HLS and that DASH does not support Apple devices; the lesson does not rely on this and calls it a simplification.
claims.verified_by: Not checked; flagged as a simplification by the author.

claims.claim_vi: Own experiment, 2026-10-19, ffmpeg 6.1.1 with libx264: 36 s synthetic video 640x360 30 fps about 800 kbit/s; HLS with 2 s segments gave 18 segments (average 230,874 bytes), with 6 s segments 6 segments (average 689,302 bytes); 12 s renditions at 300, 800, 2000 kbit/s gave 523,204; 1,344,952; 3,288,308 bytes; DASH output produced chunk-stream0-00001.m4s files and dash.mpd with a SegmentTemplate.
claims.verified_by: Commands run in the session; results copied from output.

claims.claim_vi: RFC 8216 section 6.3.3 advises a client not to pick a segment that starts less than three target durations from the end of a live playlist, so 2 s segments give a floor of about 6 s and 6 s segments about 18 s.
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge, not checked against the primary document in this session (the egress proxy allows GitHub only). Not matched against the RFC text.

design_notes_vi: Hai khung steps (4 và 3 bước) và một khung ghi chú về ba giao thức.
source_deviations: The source's eight steps are grouped into two legs, from camera to server and from server to viewer.
The lesson adds an ffmpeg experiment and a latency estimate from memory of RFC 8216, and does not repeat the source's statement about Apple devices.
